title: Film grain pass from an integer hash with luminance response
purpose: Add animated film grain to a three.js frame: triangular noise per grain cell from a 32-bit integer hash of the cell, frame and seed, mono or per channel, weighted toward the mid-tones, as a ShaderPass definition or full-screen ShaderMaterial whose every grain value the CPU mirror reproduces bit for bit.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (GLSL ES 3.00 unsigned integer arithmetic, int uniforms and the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createFilmGrainShader
exports.summary: A fresh shader definition for three.js ShaderPass or ShaderMaterial.

exports.name: createFilmGrainMaterial
exports.summary: The definition as a full-screen ShaderMaterial without depth test or write.

exports.name: grainHash
exports.signature: grainHash(x, y, frame, seed, channel) -> integer
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the shader's 32-bit cell hash.

exports.name: grainValue
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the triangular grain in (-1, 1) at an output pixel.

exports.name: grainWeight

options.name: intensity
options.meaning: Grain amplitude where the response is strongest.

options.name: response
options.meaning: 0 gives even grain; 1 makes it follow 4 L (1 - L), strongest at mid grey and gone at black and white.

options.name: grainSize
options.meaning: Grain cell size in output pixels.

options.name: colored
options.meaning: Independent grain per channel instead of mono.

options.name: frame
options.meaning: Frame number; change it every frame for moving grain.

options.name: seed
options.meaning: Another grain pattern for the same frame numbers.

limits: Stylized grain, not a model of film emulsion: square cells, a triangular value distribution and a parabolic luminance response; no grain clumping, per-layer structure or sharpening. Grain is added to the linear values the pass receives, so after sRGB encoding it looks stronger in the shadows than in the highlights. The pattern is tied to output pixels and repeats only when the frame number repeats; the frame and seed are GLSL int uniforms, limited to 2147483647. Output goes through three.js's output colour space conversion. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: 32-bit integer hash from xor-shift and multiply rounds
Triangular distribution as the sum of two uniform draws
